title: Q3 Activation Corridor: Orchestration & OKR Signal Plan for Isolated Tenancies
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description: Goal: Create an execution-ready plan that sequences activation lanes for Private/VPC/on-prem customers across Q3, maps each lane to OKR outcomes, and defines gating signals and rollback criteria. This ticket coordinates cross-functional alignment (Eng, Console, Ops, Support, Sales) and produces a playbook with runnable checklists, cohort definitions, and measurable success signals. Scope excludes feature-level implementation work (those remain in ENG tickets) but includes gating criteria, acceptance metrics, release window proposals, and customer communication templates.
objectives: Define three activation lanes (Pilot, Early Adopter, General Availability) with clear eligibility criteria
Map each lane to measurable OKR outcomes and success metrics (time-to-activate, failed-rollbacks, support load delta)
Produce a gating matrix with technical acceptance tests, performance SLO thresholds, and operational runbooks
Finalize a phased communications plan for customers and Sales enabling artifacts
acceptance_criteria: Activation lanes documented and approved by Eng, Console, and Customer Success
OKR mappings committed and surfaced in the product roadmap tracker
Gating matrix contains concrete numeric thresholds and automated checks where possible
Playbook and checklist vetted in a tabletop run with at least one Solutions Engineer and one customer success manager
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Eng, Console, Ops. Collected initial constraints on autoscaling windows and upgrade cadence.
2026-03-05: Drafted eligibility criteria for Pilot lane; sequenced customers by tenancy size and compliance risk.
2026-03-09: Eng requested tightening of performance SLOs for GA lane; added latency and KV-cache hit-rate minimums to gating matrix.
2026-03-12: Legal and Security requested an encryption key rotation checklist for private on-prem activations; added as mandatory pre-activate step.
2026-03-15: Cross-functional review scheduled; incorporated feedback on customer communication tone and rollback windows. Updated plan to include a dark-launch option for high-risk tenants.
risks: Capacity contention during early adopter surge could raise latency above SLOs
Incomplete automation for pre-activation checks increases manual toil and error surface
Customer data residency requirements may require bespoke networking work for certain tenants
Tight coordination window with Sales may cause missed activation windows if approvals lag
mitigations: Reserve burst slots in Dedicated pools for pilot activations and instrument auto-throttles
Prioritize automation of pre-activation checks (health, KMS access, upgrade compatibility) as part of the playbook
Create a fast-path exceptions process with Legal for residency edge cases
Establish a single-point activation calendar and a 'three-business-day' SLA for internal approvals
runbooks_and_playbook: Activation step-by-step (dark-launch -> gradual traffic -> monitor -> promote)
Rollback recipe (snapshot, config revert, model fallback)
Post-activation audit (SLO check, billing reconciliation, customer survey)
next_steps: Finish gating matrix and send for Eng/Console sign-off by 2026-03-22
Run a tabletop activation with Solutions Engineering and one pilot customer the week of 2026-04-04
Provide Sales with one-pager and activation checklist by 2026-04-01
Instrument dashboards to track the five defined success metrics before Pilot begins
